schema.description: {{COMPANY_NAME}} reusable Merlino Catalogue threat-profile template for System Integrator / MSP organisations. TP-06 models the complete Ransomware / Enterprise Disruption / Destructive Impact scenario: exploitation and credential-based entry, foothold/persistence, privilege escalation, Windows and cloud credential theft, internal discovery, RDP/SMB/SSH/WinRM/WMI lateral movement, RMM/tunneling, virtualization targeting, EDR/firewall/log impairment, backup and recovery destruction, double-extortion collection/exfiltration, Windows/Linux/ESXi/cloud encryption, data destruction and administrator lockout. It incorporates 2025-2026 Mandiant, MITRE Qilin/Water Galura and Storm-0501 threat context while remaining a generic reusable profile. Organisation is represented by {{COMPANY_NAME}}.

data.Name: TP-06 | Active Scanning: Vulnerability Scanning
data.Source: X3M.AI Threat Profile - System Integrator - TP-06 Ransomware / Enterprise Disruption / Destructive Impact
data.Description: Scan exposed VPN, firewall, remote-access, web, file-transfer, backup and enterprise applications for exploitable vulnerabilities. Why it matters for a system integrator/MSP: Ransomware operations are highly opportunistic around internet-facing infrastructure. Mandiant found exploitation/suspected exploitation in about one-third of 2025 ransomware incidents, particularly VPNs and firewalls. Applicability: Internet-Facing. Ransomware lifecycle phase: Pre-Intrusion. Primary assets at risk: VPN gateways, Firewalls, Citrix, SharePoint, SAP, Managed file transfer, Backup software. Detection opportunities: WAF/IDS scanning signals; High-rate vulnerability probes; Repeated requests to known vulnerable endpoints. Defensive considerations: Rapid patching; External attack-surface management; Reduce direct exposure; WAF/IPS; CISA KEV prioritisation.
data.Notes: Threat Profile TP-06 | Generic System Integrator / MSP ransomware and destructive-impact profile | Organisation placeholder: {{COMPANY_NAME}}. Inclusion rationale: Ransomware operations are highly opportunistic around internet-facing infrastructure. Mandiant found exploitation/suspected exploitation in about one-third of 2025 ransomware incidents, particularly VPNs and firewalls. Threat-led context: Mandiant 2025 ransomware investigations: exploitation/suspected exploitation was the most common identified initial access vector. Applicability=Internet-Facing; RansomwarePhase=Pre-Intrusion; Priority=High; Confidence=High. Scope boundary: TP-06 models the complete ransomware / disruptive extortion chain from perimeter or identity initial access through persistence, credential theft, privilege escalation, discovery, lateral movement, deployment, virtualization targeting, defense impairment, backup/recovery destruction, double-extortion collection/exfiltration, encryption/destruction and administrator lockout. It intentionally includes Windows, Linux, ESXi/virtualization and cloud-native ransomware paths because contemporary ransomware is no longer endpoint-only. Detailed identity-only compromise belongs to TP-01/TP-04, Partner Center/customer trusted access to TP-02/TP-03, software supply chain to TP-05, and data-theft-only/SaaS extortion is expanded in TP-09. This record is threat-profile intelligence and does not assert that the behavior occurred in a specific organisation.

data.Name: TP-06 | Gather Victim Identity Information: Credentials
data.Source: X3M.AI Threat Profile - System Integrator - TP-06 Ransomware / Enterprise Disruption / Destructive Impact
data.Description: Obtain employee, VPN, administrator or supplier credentials from infostealer logs, previous breaches, access brokers or criminal marketplaces. Why it matters for a system integrator/MSP: Stolen credentials remain a major ransomware entry path and allow attackers to bypass perimeter exploitation entirely. Applicability: Core. Ransomware lifecycle phase: Pre-Intrusion. Primary assets at risk: Employee credentials, VPN credentials, Admin credentials, Third-party credentials. Detection opportunities: Leaked credential monitoring; Identity Protection; Credential exposure intelligence. Defensive considerations: Phishing-resistant MFA; Credential rotation after exposure; No password reuse.

data.Name: TP-06 | Exploit Public-Facing Application
data.Source: X3M.AI Threat Profile - System Integrator - TP-06 Ransomware / Enterprise Disruption / Destructive Impact
data.Description: Exploit vulnerable public-facing VPNs, firewalls, Citrix, SharePoint, SAP, managed file-transfer, backup or web applications to gain code execution or authenticated access. Why it matters for a system integrator/MSP: This is a core ransomware initial-access technique. System integrators typically expose customer-support, VPN and project services and may also administer technology stacks commonly targeted by ransomware operators. Applicability: Core / Internet. Ransomware lifecycle phase: Initial Access. Primary assets at risk: VPN, Firewall, Web applications, SharePoint, SAP, Backup servers, Managed file transfer. Detection opportunities: Exploit telemetry; Web-shell creation; New process from public-facing service; Unexpected administrative session. Defensive considerations: Patch KEVs quickly; WAF/IPS; Internet exposure minimisation; Segmentation of appliances from identity/backup systems.

data.Name: TP-06 | External Remote Services
data.Source: X3M.AI Threat Profile - System Integrator - TP-06 Ransomware / Enterprise Disruption / Destructive Impact
data.Description: Use stolen or brute-forced credentials to authenticate to VPN, Citrix, VNC, externally exposed management or other remote access services. Why it matters for a system integrator/MSP: Legitimate remote services are a frequent ransomware entry mechanism and may directly place the actor inside trusted network zones. Applicability: Core. Ransomware lifecycle phase: Initial Access. Primary assets at risk: VPN, Citrix, Remote support, Management gateways. Detection opportunities: New device/location; Successful login after brute force; Access outside normal hours; Remote session followed by reconnaissance. Defensive considerations: MFA; Source restrictions; Device compliance; Named accounts; No direct admin access from VPN.
data.Notes: Threat Profile TP-06 | Generic System Integrator / MSP ransomware and destructive-impact profile | Organisation placeholder: {{COMPANY_NAME}}. Inclusion rationale: Legitimate remote services are a frequent ransomware entry mechanism and may directly place the actor inside trusted network zones. Threat-led context: Mandiant observed stolen credentials commonly used against VPN/RDP. Applicability=Core; RansomwarePhase=Initial Access; Priority=Critical; Confidence=High. Scope boundary: TP-06 models the complete ransomware / disruptive extortion chain from perimeter or identity initial access through persistence, credential theft, privilege escalation, discovery, lateral movement, deployment, virtualization targeting, defense impairment, backup/recovery destruction, double-extortion collection/exfiltration, encryption/destruction and administrator lockout. It intentionally includes Windows, Linux, ESXi/virtualization and cloud-native ransomware paths because contemporary ransomware is no longer endpoint-only. Detailed identity-only compromise belongs to TP-01/TP-04, Partner Center/customer trusted access to TP-02/TP-03, software supply chain to TP-05, and data-theft-only/SaaS extortion is expanded in TP-09. This record is threat-profile intelligence and does not assert that the behavior occurred in a specific organisation.

data.Description: Leverage an already compromised supplier, subsidiary, MSP, partner or customer trust path to enter the target environment. Why it matters for a system integrator/MSP: System integrators have reciprocal third-party risk: they may be used to reach customers, but their own suppliers, subsidiaries or partner connectivity may also become an initial ransomware path. Detection opportunities: Third-party authentication anomalies; Supplier access outside scope; Cross-environment pivot patterns. Defensive considerations: Least privilege for suppliers; Time-bound access; Network segmentation; Third-party MFA; Periodic trust review.

data.Description: Use compromised Entra/cloud accounts to access Microsoft 365, Azure and other SaaS/IaaS administration surfaces. Why it matters for a system integrator/MSP: Modern ransomware can expand from identity compromise into cloud control planes, including cloud-native extortion and destructive actions. Applicability: Cloud / Entra. Ransomware lifecycle phase: Initial Access / Cloud Pivot. Primary assets at risk: Entra ID, Azure, Microsoft 365, Cloud storage, Cloud backups. Detection opportunities: SigninLogs; Risk detections; New cloud services accessed; Privileged API activity after risky login. Defensive considerations: Phishing-resistant MFA; Conditional Access; PIM; Dedicated admin identities.
data.Notes: Threat Profile TP-06 | Generic System Integrator / MSP ransomware and destructive-impact profile | Organisation placeholder: {{COMPANY_NAME}}. Inclusion rationale: Modern ransomware can expand from identity compromise into cloud control planes, including cloud-native extortion and destructive actions. Threat-led context: Storm-0501 demonstrates ransomware/extortion operations extending into Entra and Azure. Applicability=Cloud / Entra; RansomwarePhase=Initial Access / Cloud Pivot; Priority=Critical; Confidence=High. Scope boundary: TP-06 models the complete ransomware / disruptive extortion chain from perimeter or identity initial access through persistence, credential theft, privilege escalation, discovery, lateral movement, deployment, virtualization targeting, defense impairment, backup/recovery destruction, double-extortion collection/exfiltration, encryption/destruction and administrator lockout. It intentionally includes Windows, Linux, ESXi/virtualization and cloud-native ransomware paths because contemporary ransomware is no longer endpoint-only. Detailed identity-only compromise belongs to TP-01/TP-04, Partner Center/customer trusted access to TP-02/TP-03, software supply chain to TP-05, and data-theft-only/SaaS extortion is expanded in TP-09. This record is threat-profile intelligence and does not assert that the behavior occurred in a specific organisation.

data.Name: TP-06 | Brute Force: Password Guessing
data.Source: X3M.AI Threat Profile - System Integrator - TP-06 Ransomware / Enterprise Disruption / Destructive Impact
data.Description: Guess passwords against VPN, RDP, appliances or administrative services. Why it matters for a system integrator/MSP: Ransomware actors may repeatedly attempt likely passwords against exposed authentication systems, particularly legacy or unmanaged remote access. Applicability: Remote Access. Ransomware lifecycle phase: Initial Access. Primary assets at risk: VPN, RDP, Appliances, Admin portals. Detection opportunities: Repeated failures against one account; Slow persistent password guessing. Defensive considerations: MFA; Lockout/smart lockout; Strong passwords; Rate limiting.

data.Name: TP-06 | Brute Force: Password Spraying
data.Source: X3M.AI Threat Profile - System Integrator - TP-06 Ransomware / Enterprise Disruption / Destructive Impact
data.Description: Try common passwords across many enterprise identities to obtain a working VPN, cloud or domain account. Why it matters for a system integrator/MSP: Spraying reduces per-account failure volume and remains relevant across identity providers and remote-access systems. Applicability: Core. Ransomware lifecycle phase: Initial Access. Primary assets at risk: Entra users, VPN users, Domain users. Detection opportunities: Many users targeted from common infrastructure; Distributed spray detection. Defensive considerations: MFA; Password protection; Smart lockout; Block legacy authentication.

data.Name: TP-06 | Brute Force: Credential Stuffing
data.Source: X3M.AI Threat Profile - System Integrator - TP-06 Ransomware / Enterprise Disruption / Destructive Impact
data.Description: Reuse breached username/password combinations against corporate identity, VPN and SaaS services. Why it matters for a system integrator/MSP: Infostealer and breach-derived credentials can provide silent ransomware entry if passwords are reused. Applicability: Core. Ransomware lifecycle phase: Initial Access. Primary assets at risk: VPN, Entra, SaaS, Remote services. Detection opportunities: Leaked credential correlation; Unfamiliar sign-in properties. Defensive considerations: MFA; Unique passwords; Leak monitoring.

data.Description: Send links that lead to credential theft, malicious download, remote-support abuse or payload execution. data.Name: TP-06 | Phishing: Spearphishing via Service

data.Description: Use Teams or another collaboration service to impersonate support and persuade a user to enable remote access or install a legitimate support tool. Detection opportunities: External/rare Teams sender; Quick Assist installation after chat; User-reported support impersonation. Defensive considerations: Restrict external collaboration; Verified help-desk procedures; Application control.

data.Name: TP-06 | User Execution: Malicious Link
data.Source: X3M.AI Threat Profile - System Integrator - TP-06 Ransomware / Enterprise Disruption / Destructive Impact
data.Description: Cause a user to click or launch content that results in credential theft, remote-access tooling or malware execution. Why it matters for a system integrator/MSP: User action can complete phishing-based ransomware initial access even when the final payload is delivered through legitimate software or browser flows. Applicability: User Endpoint. Ransomware lifecycle phase: Initial Access. Primary assets at risk: User browser, Endpoint, Identity session. Detection opportunities: URL click plus suspicious process/download; User execution after external lure. Defensive considerations: Web filtering; Application control; User training.
data.Notes: Threat Profile TP-06 | Generic System Integrator / MSP ransomware and destructive-impact profile | Organisation placeholder: {{COMPANY_NAME}}. Inclusion rationale: User action can complete phishing-based ransomware initial access even when the final payload is delivered through legitimate software or browser flows. Threat-led context: Technique included because it is structurally relevant to ransomware / enterprise disruption even where no specific current actor evidence is required. Applicability=User Endpoint; RansomwarePhase=Initial Access; Priority=High; Confidence=High. Scope boundary: TP-06 models the complete ransomware / disruptive extortion chain from perimeter or identity initial access through persistence, credential theft, privilege escalation, discovery, lateral movement, deployment, virtualization targeting, defense impairment, backup/recovery destruction, double-extortion collection/exfiltration, encryption/destruction and administrator lockout. It intentionally includes Windows, Linux, ESXi/virtualization and cloud-native ransomware paths because contemporary ransomware is no longer endpoint-only. Detailed identity-only compromise belongs to TP-01/TP-04, Partner Center/customer trusted access to TP-02/TP-03, software supply chain to TP-05, and data-theft-only/SaaS extortion is expanded in TP-09. This record is threat-profile intelligence and does not assert that the behavior occurred in a specific organisation.

data.Name: TP-06 | Remote Access Tools: Remote Desktop Software
data.Source: X3M.AI Threat Profile - System Integrator - TP-06 Ransomware / Enterprise Disruption / Destructive Impact
data.Description: Install or abuse legitimate remote management software such as AnyDesk, ScreenConnect, Splashtop or similar tools. Why it matters for a system integrator/MSP: RMM tools are trusted, digitally signed and designed for administration, making them effective for resilient ransomware access and difficult to distinguish from support activity. Applicability: Core. Ransomware lifecycle phase: Foothold / Persistence. Primary assets at risk: Endpoints, Servers, RMM consoles, Managed-service systems. Detection opportunities: New RMM installation; Remote session outside approved ticket/change; New operator/source. Defensive considerations: Allow-list approved RMM; MFA; Session logging; Application control; Tie sessions to tickets.

data.Name: TP-06 | Create Account: Local Account
data.Source: X3M.AI Threat Profile - System Integrator - TP-06 Ransomware / Enterprise Disruption / Destructive Impact
data.Description: Create a local account to retain administrative access to a host or appliance. Why it matters for a system integrator/MSP: Attacker-created local admins provide a simple fallback if domain credentials or remote tooling are remediated. Applicability: Windows/Linux. Ransomware lifecycle phase: Foothold / Persistence. Primary assets at risk: Servers, Workstations, ESXi/appliances. Detection opportunities: New local user; Immediate admin group assignment; Account created outside provisioning. Defensive considerations: Local account governance; LAPS; Alert on new administrators.
data.Notes: Threat Profile TP-06 | Generic System Integrator / MSP ransomware and destructive-impact profile | Organisation placeholder: {{COMPANY_NAME}}. Inclusion rationale: Attacker-created local admins provide a simple fallback if domain credentials or remote tooling are remediated. Threat-led context: Mandiant observed attacker-created accounts used for lateral movement. Applicability=Windows/Linux; RansomwarePhase=Foothold / Persistence; Priority=High; Confidence=High. Scope boundary: TP-06 models the complete ransomware / disruptive extortion chain from perimeter or identity initial access through persistence, credential theft, privilege escalation, discovery, lateral movement, deployment, virtualization targeting, defense impairment, backup/recovery destruction, double-extortion collection/exfiltration, encryption/destruction and administrator lockout. It intentionally includes Windows, Linux, ESXi/virtualization and cloud-native ransomware paths because contemporary ransomware is no longer endpoint-only. Detailed identity-only compromise belongs to TP-01/TP-04, Partner Center/customer trusted access to TP-02/TP-03, software supply chain to TP-05, and data-theft-only/SaaS extortion is expanded in TP-09. This record is threat-profile intelligence and does not assert that the behavior occurred in a specific organisation.

data.Description: Create a domain account and grant it privileges for persistent access. data.Name: TP-06 | Account Manipulation: Additional Local or Domain Groups
data.Source: X3M.AI Threat Profile - System Integrator - TP-06 Ransomware / Enterprise Disruption / Destructive Impact
data.Description: Add attacker-controlled or compromised accounts to local or domain administrator, RDP, VPN or equivalent privileged groups. Why it matters for a system integrator/MSP: Administrative group membership enables credential access, defense disabling and enterprise-wide ransomware deployment. Applicability: AD / Endpoint. Ransomware lifecycle phase: Privilege Escalation / Persistence. Primary assets at risk: Local Administrators, Domain Admins, Remote Desktop Users, VPN groups. Detection opportunities: Privileged group membership changes; New administrator after suspicious authentication. Defensive considerations: PAM/JIT; Alert on privileged group change; Minimise standing admins.
data.Notes: Threat Profile TP-06 | Generic System Integrator / MSP ransomware and destructive-impact profile | Organisation placeholder: {{COMPANY_NAME}}. Inclusion rationale: Administrative group membership enables credential access, defense disabling and enterprise-wide ransomware deployment. Threat-led context: Mandiant observed routine addition of compromised/created accounts to administrator groups. Applicability=AD / Endpoint; RansomwarePhase=Privilege Escalation / Persistence; Priority=Critical; Confidence=High. Scope boundary: TP-06 models the complete ransomware / disruptive extortion chain from perimeter or identity initial access through persistence, credential theft, privilege escalation, discovery, lateral movement, deployment, virtualization targeting, defense impairment, backup/recovery destruction, double-extortion collection/exfiltration, encryption/destruction and administrator lockout. It intentionally includes Windows, Linux, ESXi/virtualization and cloud-native ransomware paths because contemporary ransomware is no longer endpoint-only. Detailed identity-only compromise belongs to TP-01/TP-04, Partner Center/customer trusted access to TP-02/TP-03, software supply chain to TP-05, and data-theft-only/SaaS extortion is expanded in TP-09. This record is threat-profile intelligence and does not assert that the behavior occurred in a specific organisation.

data.Name: TP-06 | Boot or Logon Autostart Execution: Registry Run Keys / Startup Folder
data.Source: X3M.AI Threat Profile - System Integrator - TP-06 Ransomware / Enterprise Disruption / Destructive Impact
data.Description: Create Run/RunOnce registry entries or startup persistence for ransomware or precursors. Why it matters for a system integrator/MSP: Registry autostart can ensure payload execution across reboot or multiple systems and is documented for Qilin/Agenda activity. Applicability: Windows. Ransomware lifecycle phase: Persistence / Deployment. Primary assets at risk: Windows endpoints, Servers. Detection opportunities: New Run/RunOnce entries; Payload launched from Public/Temp/AppData. Defensive considerations: Registry monitoring; EDR; Application control.
data.Notes: Threat Profile TP-06 | Generic System Integrator / MSP ransomware and destructive-impact profile | Organisation placeholder: {{COMPANY_NAME}}. Inclusion rationale: Registry autostart can ensure payload execution across reboot or multiple systems and is documented for Qilin/Agenda activity. Threat-led context: MITRE documents Qilin creating RunOnce autostart. Applicability=Windows; RansomwarePhase=Persistence / Deployment; Priority=High; Confidence=High. Scope boundary: TP-06 models the complete ransomware / disruptive extortion chain from perimeter or identity initial access through persistence, credential theft, privilege escalation, discovery, lateral movement, deployment, virtualization targeting, defense impairment, backup/recovery destruction, double-extortion collection/exfiltration, encryption/destruction and administrator lockout. It intentionally includes Windows, Linux, ESXi/virtualization and cloud-native ransomware paths because contemporary ransomware is no longer endpoint-only. Detailed identity-only compromise belongs to TP-01/TP-04, Partner Center/customer trusted access to TP-02/TP-03, software supply chain to TP-05, and data-theft-only/SaaS extortion is expanded in TP-09. This record is threat-profile intelligence and does not assert that the behavior occurred in a specific organisation.

data.Description: Modify Group Policy to push scheduled tasks, scripts, security exclusions or ransomware across domain systems. Defensive considerations: Tier 0 administration; GPO change approval; Alert on GPO modifications.

data.Name: TP-06 | Account Manipulation: Additional Cloud Credentials
data.Source: X3M.AI Threat Profile - System Integrator - TP-06 Ransomware / Enterprise Disruption / Destructive Impact
data.Description: Add attacker-controlled secret/certificate to an application, service principal or cloud identity. Why it matters for a system integrator/MSP: This can preserve cloud control even after the initial human identity is reset and can support later destructive cloud actions. Applicability: Cloud. Ransomware lifecycle phase: Cloud Persistence. Primary assets at risk: Service principals, Applications, Automation identities. Detection opportunities: New app credential; Certificate/secret addition after risky sign-in. Defensive considerations: Workload identity federation; Managed identities; Alert on credential changes.

data.Description: Export or read SAM/SYSTEM/SECURITY registry data to obtain local password hashes and secrets. data.Name: TP-06 | OS Credential Dumping: DCSync
data.Source: X3M.AI Threat Profile - System Integrator - TP-06 Ransomware / Enterprise Disruption / Destructive Impact
data.Description: Abuse AD replication privileges to retrieve credential data including highly privileged account hashes. Why it matters for a system integrator/MSP: DCSync can convert elevated directory privilege into domain-wide credential compromise without touching LSASS on the DC. Applicability: Active Directory. Ransomware lifecycle phase: Credential Access. Primary assets at risk: Domain controller replication, KRBTGT, Domain admins. Detection opportunities: Replication requests from non-DC; Unusual replication rights. Defensive considerations: Restrict replication privileges; MDI; Tier 0 governance.
data.Notes: Threat Profile TP-06 | Generic System Integrator / MSP ransomware and destructive-impact profile | Organisation placeholder: {{COMPANY_NAME}}. Inclusion rationale: DCSync can convert elevated directory privilege into domain-wide credential compromise without touching LSASS on the DC. Threat-led context: Mandiant observed abuse of AD replication/DCSync in ransomware intrusions. Applicability=Active Directory; RansomwarePhase=Credential Access; Priority=Critical; Confidence=High. Scope boundary: TP-06 models the complete ransomware / disruptive extortion chain from perimeter or identity initial access through persistence, credential theft, privilege escalation, discovery, lateral movement, deployment, virtualization targeting, defense impairment, backup/recovery destruction, double-extortion collection/exfiltration, encryption/destruction and administrator lockout. It intentionally includes Windows, Linux, ESXi/virtualization and cloud-native ransomware paths because contemporary ransomware is no longer endpoint-only. Detailed identity-only compromise belongs to TP-01/TP-04, Partner Center/customer trusted access to TP-02/TP-03, software supply chain to TP-05, and data-theft-only/SaaS extortion is expanded in TP-09. This record is threat-profile intelligence and does not assert that the behavior occurred in a specific organisation.

data.Description: Request service tickets and crack them offline to obtain service-account passwords. data.Name: TP-06 | Credentials from Password Stores: Windows Credential Manager
data.Source: X3M.AI Threat Profile - System Integrator - TP-06 Ransomware / Enterprise Disruption / Destructive Impact
data.Description: Extract credentials from Windows Credential Manager and related DPAPI-protected stores. Why it matters for a system integrator/MSP: Stored remote-service and administrative credentials can support rapid ransomware lateral movement. Applicability: Windows. Ransomware lifecycle phase: Credential Access. Primary assets at risk: Windows Credential Manager, RDP credentials, Administrative workstation. Detection opportunities: Vault access by unusual processes; Credential dumping alerts. Defensive considerations: Credential Guard; PAW; No stored privileged credentials.
data.Notes: Threat Profile TP-06 | Generic System Integrator / MSP ransomware and destructive-impact profile | Organisation placeholder: {{COMPANY_NAME}}. Inclusion rationale: Stored remote-service and administrative credentials can support rapid ransomware lateral movement. Threat-led context: Technique included because it is structurally relevant to ransomware / enterprise disruption even where no specific current actor evidence is required. Applicability=Windows; RansomwarePhase=Credential Access; Priority=High; Confidence=High. Scope boundary: TP-06 models the complete ransomware / disruptive extortion chain from perimeter or identity initial access through persistence, credential theft, privilege escalation, discovery, lateral movement, deployment, virtualization targeting, defense impairment, backup/recovery destruction, double-extortion collection/exfiltration, encryption/destruction and administrator lockout. data.Name: TP-06 | Unsecured Credentials: Credentials In Files
data.Source: X3M.AI Threat Profile - System Integrator - TP-06 Ransomware / Enterprise Disruption / Destructive Impact
data.Description: Search configuration, scripts, documentation, backup scripts and shares for plaintext credentials and keys. Why it matters for a system integrator/MSP: Mandiant observed ransomware actors targeting credentials stored in cleartext and searching backup-related files. Applicability: Core. Ransomware lifecycle phase: Credential Access. Primary assets at risk: Scripts, Config files, Documentation, Backup scripts. Detection opportunities: Secret-pattern search; Bulk reads of configuration files. Defensive considerations: Secret scanning; Central secrets management; No plaintext passwords.
data.Notes: Threat Profile TP-06 | Generic System Integrator / MSP ransomware and destructive-impact profile | Organisation placeholder: {{COMPANY_NAME}}. Inclusion rationale: Mandiant observed ransomware actors targeting credentials stored in cleartext and searching backup-related files. Threat-led context: Cleartext credential harvesting is observed in ransomware investigations. Applicability=Core; RansomwarePhase=Credential Access; Priority=Critical; Confidence=High. Scope boundary: TP-06 models the complete ransomware / disruptive extortion chain from perimeter or identity initial access through persistence, credential theft, privilege escalation, discovery, lateral movement, deployment, virtualization targeting, defense impairment, backup/recovery destruction, double-extortion collection/exfiltration, encryption/destruction and administrator lockout. It intentionally includes Windows, Linux, ESXi/virtualization and cloud-native ransomware paths because contemporary ransomware is no longer endpoint-only. Detailed identity-only compromise belongs to TP-01/TP-04, Partner Center/customer trusted access to TP-02/TP-03, software supply chain to TP-05, and data-theft-only/SaaS extortion is expanded in TP-09. This record is threat-profile intelligence and does not assert that the behavior occurred in a specific organisation.

data.Name: TP-06 | System Network Configuration Discovery
data.Source: X3M.AI Threat Profile - System Integrator - TP-06 Ransomware / Enterprise Disruption / Destructive Impact
data.Description: Collect IP, routes, DNS, adapters and network configuration. Why it matters for a system integrator/MSP: Local network information helps actors identify reachable management zones and lateral paths. Applicability: Core. Ransomware lifecycle phase: Internal Reconnaissance. Primary assets at risk: Network adapters, Routes, DNS, Subnets. Detection opportunities: ipconfig/ifconfig/route commands within ransomware chain. Defensive considerations: Behavioral detection.
data.Notes: Threat Profile TP-06 | Generic System Integrator / MSP ransomware and destructive-impact profile | Organisation placeholder: {{COMPANY_NAME}}. Inclusion rationale: Local network information helps actors identify reachable management zones and lateral paths. Threat-led context: Mandiant observed ipconfig and related native tools; Qilin performs network configuration discovery. Applicability=Core; RansomwarePhase=Internal Reconnaissance; Priority=High; Confidence=High. Scope boundary: TP-06 models the complete ransomware / disruptive extortion chain from perimeter or identity initial access through persistence, credential theft, privilege escalation, discovery, lateral movement, deployment, virtualization targeting, defense impairment, backup/recovery destruction, double-extortion collection/exfiltration, encryption/destruction and administrator lockout. It intentionally includes Windows, Linux, ESXi/virtualization and cloud-native ransomware paths because contemporary ransomware is no longer endpoint-only. Detailed identity-only compromise belongs to TP-01/TP-04, Partner Center/customer trusted access to TP-02/TP-03, software supply chain to TP-05, and data-theft-only/SaaS extortion is expanded in TP-09. This record is threat-profile intelligence and does not assert that the behavior occurred in a specific organisation.

data.Name: TP-06 | Network Share Discovery

data.Description: Enumerate SMB/network shares and mounted resources. Defensive considerations: Share ACL least privilege; Segmentation; Monitor enumeration.

data.Name: TP-06 | Process Discovery
data.Source: X3M.AI Threat Profile - System Integrator - TP-06 Ransomware / Enterprise Disruption / Destructive Impact
data.Description: Enumerate running processes to identify security agents, backup software, databases and applications whose files may be locked. Why it matters for a system integrator/MSP: Process discovery supports both defense impairment and preparation for encryption. Applicability: Core. Ransomware lifecycle phase: Internal Reconnaissance. Primary assets at risk: EDR processes, Backup agents, Database processes, Business applications. Detection opportunities: tasklist/Get-Process from suspicious admin context. Defensive considerations: Behavioral detection.
data.Notes: Threat Profile TP-06 | Generic System Integrator / MSP ransomware and destructive-impact profile | Organisation placeholder: {{COMPANY_NAME}}. Inclusion rationale: Process discovery supports both defense impairment and preparation for encryption. Threat-led context: Qilin performs process discovery. Applicability=Core; RansomwarePhase=Internal Reconnaissance; Priority=High; Confidence=High. Scope boundary: TP-06 models the complete ransomware / disruptive extortion chain from perimeter or identity initial access through persistence, credential theft, privilege escalation, discovery, lateral movement, deployment, virtualization targeting, defense impairment, backup/recovery destruction, double-extortion collection/exfiltration, encryption/destruction and administrator lockout. It intentionally includes Windows, Linux, ESXi/virtualization and cloud-native ransomware paths because contemporary ransomware is no longer endpoint-only. Detailed identity-only compromise belongs to TP-01/TP-04, Partner Center/customer trusted access to TP-02/TP-03, software supply chain to TP-05, and data-theft-only/SaaS extortion is expanded in TP-09. This record is threat-profile intelligence and does not assert that the behavior occurred in a specific organisation.

data.Name: TP-06 | Software Discovery: Backup Software Discovery
data.Source: X3M.AI Threat Profile - System Integrator - TP-06 Ransomware / Enterprise Disruption / Destructive Impact
data.Description: Enumerate backup software, services, configuration and recovery tooling such as Veeam, Commvault or Cohesity. Why it matters for a system integrator/MSP: Backup systems are ransomware crown jewels. Actors discover them to steal credentials, delete backups and prevent recovery. Applicability: Core. Ransomware lifecycle phase: Pre-Impact Discovery. Primary assets at risk: Veeam, Commvault, Cohesity, Backup agents, Recovery consoles. Detection opportunities: Queries for backup products/services; Registry/process inspection targeting backup software. Defensive considerations: Isolate backup plane; Separate backup identities; Immutable backups; Alert on backup discovery.
data.Notes: Threat Profile TP-06 | Generic System Integrator / MSP ransomware and destructive-impact profile | Organisation placeholder: {{COMPANY_NAME}}. Inclusion rationale: Backup systems are ransomware crown jewels. Actors discover them to steal credentials, delete backups and prevent recovery. Threat-led context: Mandiant emphasizes deliberate targeting of backup infrastructure; ATT&CK added Backup Software Discovery T1518.002. Applicability=Core; RansomwarePhase=Pre-Impact Discovery; Priority=Critical; Confidence=High. Scope boundary: TP-06 models the complete ransomware / disruptive extortion chain from perimeter or identity initial access through persistence, credential theft, privilege escalation, discovery, lateral movement, deployment, virtualization targeting, defense impairment, backup/recovery destruction, double-extortion collection/exfiltration, encryption/destruction and administrator lockout. It intentionally includes Windows, Linux, ESXi/virtualization and cloud-native ransomware paths because contemporary ransomware is no longer endpoint-only. Detailed identity-only compromise belongs to TP-01/TP-04, Partner Center/customer trusted access to TP-02/TP-03, software supply chain to TP-05, and data-theft-only/SaaS extortion is expanded in TP-09. This record is threat-profile intelligence and does not assert that the behavior occurred in a specific organisation.

data.Description: Enumerate virtual machines through vCenter, ESXi CLI, Hyper-V tooling or management consoles. data.Name: TP-06 | Local Storage Discovery
data.Source: X3M.AI Threat Profile - System Integrator - TP-06 Ransomware / Enterprise Disruption / Destructive Impact
data.Description: Enumerate local disks, mounted volumes and storage locations. Why it matters for a system integrator/MSP: Ransomware selects which drives and resources to encrypt and may exclude system-critical paths needed to keep the host running long enough to finish encryption. Applicability: Core. Ransomware lifecycle phase: Pre-Impact Discovery. Primary assets at risk: Local disks, Mounted volumes, NAS mounts. Detection opportunities: Drive enumeration shortly before encryption. Defensive considerations: Behavioral ransomware detection.

data.Name: TP-06 | System Service Discovery

data.Description: Enumerate system services to identify security, backup, database and business services. Why it matters for a system integrator/MSP: Service discovery precedes stopping services so files can be encrypted and protections disabled. Applicability: Windows / Linux. Ransomware lifecycle phase: Pre-Impact Discovery. Primary assets at risk: Windows/Linux services, Backup agents, Databases. Detection opportunities: sc query / Get-Service / systemctl enumeration. Defensive considerations: Behavioral detection.

data.Name: TP-06 | Cloud Service Dashboard
data.Source: X3M.AI Threat Profile - System Integrator - TP-06 Ransomware / Enterprise Disruption / Destructive Impact
data.Description: Use cloud dashboards to inspect subscriptions, identities, storage, backup and security configuration. Why it matters for a system integrator/MSP: Interactive ransomware operators can use legitimate portals to identify high-impact cloud targets. Applicability: Cloud. Ransomware lifecycle phase: Cloud Discovery. Primary assets at risk: Azure portal, Entra admin center, M365 portals. Detection opportunities: Admin portal access from new device/location; Unusual resource navigation. Defensive considerations: PIM; Conditional Access; PAW.
data.Notes: Threat Profile TP-06 | Generic System Integrator / MSP ransomware and destructive-impact profile | Organisation placeholder: {{COMPANY_NAME}}. Inclusion rationale: Interactive ransomware operators can use legitimate portals to identify high-impact cloud targets. Threat-led context: Technique included because it is structurally relevant to ransomware / enterprise disruption even where no specific current actor evidence is required. Applicability=Cloud; RansomwarePhase=Cloud Discovery; Priority=High; Confidence=High. Scope boundary: TP-06 models the complete ransomware / disruptive extortion chain from perimeter or identity initial access through persistence, credential theft, privilege escalation, discovery, lateral movement, deployment, virtualization targeting, defense impairment, backup/recovery destruction, double-extortion collection/exfiltration, encryption/destruction and administrator lockout. It intentionally includes Windows, Linux, ESXi/virtualization and cloud-native ransomware paths because contemporary ransomware is no longer endpoint-only. Detailed identity-only compromise belongs to TP-01/TP-04, Partner Center/customer trusted access to TP-02/TP-03, software supply chain to TP-05, and data-theft-only/SaaS extortion is expanded in TP-09. This record is threat-profile intelligence and does not assert that the behavior occurred in a specific organisation.

data.Name: TP-06 | Remote Services: Remote Desktop Protocol
data.Source: X3M.AI Threat Profile - System Integrator - TP-06 Ransomware / Enterprise Disruption / Destructive Impact
data.Description: Use compromised or attacker-created accounts to move interactively between Windows systems. Why it matters for a system integrator/MSP: RDP was observed by Mandiant in approximately 85% of 2025 ransomware intrusions, making it one of the most important lateral-movement techniques in this profile. Applicability: Core / Windows. Ransomware lifecycle phase: Lateral Movement. Primary assets at risk: Windows endpoints, Servers, Jump hosts, Domain controllers. Detection opportunities: RDP from new sources; Admin account accessing many hosts; Off-hours RDP. Defensive considerations: MFA/gateway; Segmentation; PAW; Limit RDP.
data.Notes: Threat Profile TP-06 | Generic System Integrator / MSP ransomware and destructive-impact profile | Organisation placeholder: {{COMPANY_NAME}}. Inclusion rationale: RDP was observed by Mandiant in approximately 85% of 2025 ransomware intrusions, making it one of the most important lateral-movement techniques in this profile. Threat-led context: Mandiant observed RDP in approximately 85% of 2025 ransomware intrusions. Applicability=Core / Windows; RansomwarePhase=Lateral Movement; Priority=Critical; Confidence=High. Scope boundary: TP-06 models the complete ransomware / disruptive extortion chain from perimeter or identity initial access through persistence, credential theft, privilege escalation, discovery, lateral movement, deployment, virtualization targeting, defense impairment, backup/recovery destruction, double-extortion collection/exfiltration, encryption/destruction and administrator lockout. It intentionally includes Windows, Linux, ESXi/virtualization and cloud-native ransomware paths because contemporary ransomware is no longer endpoint-only. Detailed identity-only compromise belongs to TP-01/TP-04, Partner Center/customer trusted access to TP-02/TP-03, software supply chain to TP-05, and data-theft-only/SaaS extortion is expanded in TP-09. This record is threat-profile intelligence and does not assert that the behavior occurred in a specific organisation.

data.Description: Use SMB and administrative shares to access remote systems, stage ransomware and execute commands. data.Name: TP-06 | Remote Services: SSH
data.Source: X3M.AI Threat Profile - System Integrator - TP-06 Ransomware / Enterprise Disruption / Destructive Impact
data.Description: Use SSH to move to Linux servers, appliances and ESXi hypervisors. Why it matters for a system integrator/MSP: Mandiant observed PuTTY/KiTTY and SSH as common routes to ESXi before ransomware deployment. Applicability: Linux / ESXi. Ransomware lifecycle phase: Lateral Movement / Virtualization. Primary assets at risk: Linux, ESXi, Appliances. Detection opportunities: New SSH source/key; root login from unusual host; SSH enabled immediately before access. Defensive considerations: Management VLAN; Short-lived keys; MFA where possible; No shared root credentials.

data.Name: TP-06 | Remote Services: Windows Remote Management
data.Source: X3M.AI Threat Profile - System Integrator - TP-06 Ransomware / Enterprise Disruption / Destructive Impact
data.Description: Use WinRM/PowerShell Remoting to execute commands remotely. Why it matters for a system integrator/MSP: WinRM is repeatedly observed in ransomware operations for domain-controller and server movement using valid credentials. Applicability: Windows. Ransomware lifecycle phase: Lateral Movement. Primary assets at risk: Windows servers, Domain controllers. Detection opportunities: wsmprovhost activity; Enter-PSSession from unusual source. Defensive considerations: Restrict WinRM; JEA/JIT; Management segmentation.
data.Notes: Threat Profile TP-06 | Generic System Integrator / MSP ransomware and destructive-impact profile | Organisation placeholder: {{COMPANY_NAME}}. Inclusion rationale: WinRM is repeatedly observed in ransomware operations for domain-controller and server movement using valid credentials. Threat-led context: Mandiant observed WinRM and Enter-PSSession in ransomware intrusions. Applicability=Windows; RansomwarePhase=Lateral Movement; Priority=High; Confidence=High. Scope boundary: TP-06 models the complete ransomware / disruptive extortion chain from perimeter or identity initial access through persistence, credential theft, privilege escalation, discovery, lateral movement, deployment, virtualization targeting, defense impairment, backup/recovery destruction, double-extortion collection/exfiltration, encryption/destruction and administrator lockout. It intentionally includes Windows, Linux, ESXi/virtualization and cloud-native ransomware paths because contemporary ransomware is no longer endpoint-only. Detailed identity-only compromise belongs to TP-01/TP-04, Partner Center/customer trusted access to TP-02/TP-03, software supply chain to TP-05, and data-theft-only/SaaS extortion is expanded in TP-09. This record is threat-profile intelligence and does not assert that the behavior occurred in a specific organisation.

data.Name: TP-06 | Exploitation of Remote Services
data.Source: X3M.AI Threat Profile - System Integrator - TP-06 Ransomware / Enterprise Disruption / Destructive Impact
data.Description: Exploit vulnerabilities in internal services to gain access to additional systems. Why it matters for a system integrator/MSP: After initial entry, vulnerable internal services and management appliances can provide additional paths toward domain, backup or virtualization infrastructure. Applicability: Core. Ransomware lifecycle phase: Lateral Movement. Primary assets at risk: Internal applications, Management services, ESXi, Appliances. Detection opportunities: Exploit traffic east-west; New service process after remote request. Defensive considerations: Internal patching; Segmentation; Vulnerability management.
data.Notes: Threat Profile TP-06 | Generic System Integrator / MSP ransomware and destructive-impact profile | Organisation placeholder: {{COMPANY_NAME}}. Inclusion rationale: After initial entry, vulnerable internal services and management appliances can provide additional paths toward domain, backup or virtualization infrastructure. Threat-led context: Mandiant observed exploitation including ESXi-related privilege paths. Applicability=Core; RansomwarePhase=Lateral Movement; Priority=High; Confidence=High. Scope boundary: TP-06 models the complete ransomware / disruptive extortion chain from perimeter or identity initial access through persistence, credential theft, privilege escalation, discovery, lateral movement, deployment, virtualization targeting, defense impairment, backup/recovery destruction, double-extortion collection/exfiltration, encryption/destruction and administrator lockout. It intentionally includes Windows, Linux, ESXi/virtualization and cloud-native ransomware paths because contemporary ransomware is no longer endpoint-only. Detailed identity-only compromise belongs to TP-01/TP-04, Partner Center/customer trusted access to TP-02/TP-03, software supply chain to TP-05, and data-theft-only/SaaS extortion is expanded in TP-09. This record is threat-profile intelligence and does not assert that the behavior occurred in a specific organisation.

data.Description: Transfer ransomware encryptors, scanning tools, scripts or C2 utilities between systems. Why it matters for a system integrator/MSP: Enterprise-wide deployment requires moving tools to target servers, endpoints and hypervisors. Applicability: Core. Ransomware lifecycle phase: Deployment. Primary assets at risk: Endpoints, Servers, ESXi, Domain controllers. Detection opportunities: Executable copied to many hosts; SMB/SCP transfer shortly before execution. Defensive considerations: EDR; File reputation; Admin share monitoring.
data.Notes: Threat Profile TP-06 | Generic System Integrator / MSP ransomware and destructive-impact profile | Organisation placeholder: {{COMPANY_NAME}}. Inclusion rationale: Enterprise-wide deployment requires moving tools to target servers, endpoints and hypervisors. Threat-led context: Qilin uses PsExec for lateral tool transfer; Mandiant saw SMB/SCP staging. Applicability=Core; RansomwarePhase=Deployment; Priority=Critical; Confidence=High. Scope boundary: TP-06 models the complete ransomware / disruptive extortion chain from perimeter or identity initial access through persistence, credential theft, privilege escalation, discovery, lateral movement, deployment, virtualization targeting, defense impairment, backup/recovery destruction, double-extortion collection/exfiltration, encryption/destruction and administrator lockout. It intentionally includes Windows, Linux, ESXi/virtualization and cloud-native ransomware paths because contemporary ransomware is no longer endpoint-only. Detailed identity-only compromise belongs to TP-01/TP-04, Partner Center/customer trusted access to TP-02/TP-03, software supply chain to TP-05, and data-theft-only/SaaS extortion is expanded in TP-09. This record is threat-profile intelligence and does not assert that the behavior occurred in a specific organisation.

data.Name: TP-06 | Command and Scripting Interpreter: Cloud API
data.Source: X3M.AI Threat Profile - System Integrator - TP-06 Ransomware / Enterprise Disruption / Destructive Impact
data.Description: Use Microsoft Graph, Azure APIs, CLI or PowerShell modules with privileged cloud identities. Why it matters for a system integrator/MSP: Cloud-native ransomware can steal data, alter identity, delete backups and manipulate storage entirely through legitimate APIs. Applicability: Cloud. Ransomware lifecycle phase: Cloud Execution. Primary assets at risk: Azure, Entra, Cloud storage, Backup APIs. Detection opportunities: Unusual destructive API sequences; Bulk delete/write after privilege escalation. Defensive considerations: PIM; API behavior analytics; Protected backup roles.
data.Notes: Threat Profile TP-06 | Generic System Integrator / MSP ransomware and destructive-impact profile | Organisation placeholder: {{COMPANY_NAME}}. data.Name: TP-06 | Command and Scripting Interpreter: Hypervisor CLI

data.Description: Use hypervisor command-line interfaces such as esxcli or vim-cmd to enumerate VMs, change security settings, stop workloads and execute ransomware. Defensive considerations: Isolate hypervisor management; Dedicated credentials; MFA through vCenter where possible; Command auditing.

data.Name: TP-06 | Application Layer Protocol: Web Protocols
data.Source: X3M.AI Threat Profile - System Integrator - TP-06 Ransomware / Enterprise Disruption / Destructive Impact
data.Description: Use HTTP/HTTPS for C2, downloads or data transfer. Why it matters for a system integrator/MSP: Web protocols blend with normal enterprise traffic and support both custom malware and public tunneling frameworks. Applicability: Core. Ransomware lifecycle phase: Command and Control. Primary assets at risk: Endpoints, Servers, Proxy, Internet. Detection opportunities: Periodic HTTPS from non-browser process; New domains; Large POST after staging. Defensive considerations: Proxy; TLS/domain monitoring; Egress allow-list for critical servers.
data.Notes: Threat Profile TP-06 | Generic System Integrator / MSP ransomware and destructive-impact profile | Organisation placeholder: {{COMPANY_NAME}}. Inclusion rationale: Web protocols blend with normal enterprise traffic and support both custom malware and public tunneling frameworks. Threat-led context: Technique included because it is structurally relevant to ransomware / enterprise disruption even where no specific current actor evidence is required. Applicability=Core; RansomwarePhase=Command and Control; Priority=High; Confidence=High. Scope boundary: TP-06 models the complete ransomware / disruptive extortion chain from perimeter or identity initial access through persistence, credential theft, privilege escalation, discovery, lateral movement, deployment, virtualization targeting, defense impairment, backup/recovery destruction, double-extortion collection/exfiltration, encryption/destruction and administrator lockout. It intentionally includes Windows, Linux, ESXi/virtualization and cloud-native ransomware paths because contemporary ransomware is no longer endpoint-only. Detailed identity-only compromise belongs to TP-01/TP-04, Partner Center/customer trusted access to TP-02/TP-03, software supply chain to TP-05, and data-theft-only/SaaS extortion is expanded in TP-09. This record is threat-profile intelligence and does not assert that the behavior occurred in a specific organisation.

data.Name: TP-06 | Proxy: Multi-hop Proxy
data.Source: X3M.AI Threat Profile - System Integrator - TP-06 Ransomware / Enterprise Disruption / Destructive Impact
data.Description: Route C2 or exfiltration through multiple proxy layers or anonymization infrastructure. Why it matters for a system integrator/MSP: Multi-hop paths can complicate attribution and network blocking during extortion operations. Applicability: Core. Ransomware lifecycle phase: Command and Control. Primary assets at risk: Internet egress, C2. Detection opportunities: Connections to anonymization/proxy infrastructure. Defensive considerations: Threat-intel blocking; Egress proxy.
data.Notes: Threat Profile TP-06 | Generic System Integrator / MSP ransomware and destructive-impact profile | Organisation placeholder: {{COMPANY_NAME}}. Inclusion rationale: Multi-hop paths can complicate attribution and network blocking during extortion operations. Threat-led context: Water Galura/Qilin uses Tor-hosted leak infrastructure. Applicability=Core; RansomwarePhase=Command and Control; Priority=Medium; Confidence=Medium. Scope boundary: TP-06 models the complete ransomware / disruptive extortion chain from perimeter or identity initial access through persistence, credential theft, privilege escalation, discovery, lateral movement, deployment, virtualization targeting, defense impairment, backup/recovery destruction, double-extortion collection/exfiltration, encryption/destruction and administrator lockout. It intentionally includes Windows, Linux, ESXi/virtualization and cloud-native ransomware paths because contemporary ransomware is no longer endpoint-only. Detailed identity-only compromise belongs to TP-01/TP-04, Partner Center/customer trusted access to TP-02/TP-03, software supply chain to TP-05, and data-theft-only/SaaS extortion is expanded in TP-09. This record is threat-profile intelligence and does not assert that the behavior occurred in a specific organisation.

data.Name: TP-06 | Disable or Modify Tools
data.Source: X3M.AI Threat Profile - System Integrator - TP-06 Ransomware / Enterprise Disruption / Destructive Impact
data.Description: Terminate, disable, exclude or reconfigure security tools so ransomware can execute without interruption. Why it matters for a system integrator/MSP: Defense impairment is a consistent pre-encryption action. Ransomware operators commonly disable Defender, EDR and other security products before deployment. Applicability: Core. Ransomware lifecycle phase: Pre-Impact Defense Impairment. Primary assets at risk: EDR, Antivirus, Monitoring agents, Security tools. Detection opportunities: Security service termination; Policy/exclusion changes; Tamper events. Defensive considerations: Tamper protection; Separate security admin; PIM; Alert on agent health.

data.Description: Disable or alter cloud logging and audit integrations before destructive cloud actions. Detection opportunities: Audit configuration changes; Log ingestion gap; Admin disabling diagnostic settings. Defensive considerations: Separate log admin; Protected external SIEM; Alert on logging changes.

data.Name: TP-06 | Disable or Modify Tools: Clear Windows Event Logs
data.Source: X3M.AI Threat Profile - System Integrator - TP-06 Ransomware / Enterprise Disruption / Destructive Impact
data.Description: Clear Windows event logs to remove traces of remote access, credentials, commands and deployment. Why it matters for a system integrator/MSP: Log clearing is routinely observed before or after ransomware impact and is directly supported by Qilin. Applicability: Windows. Ransomware lifecycle phase: Defense Impairment. Primary assets at risk: Windows event logs, PowerShell logs. Detection opportunities: wevtutil/clear-log; Log clear audit events. Defensive considerations: Forward logs off-host; SIEM retention; Alert on clearing.
data.Notes: Threat Profile TP-06 | Generic System Integrator / MSP ransomware and destructive-impact profile | Organisation placeholder: {{COMPANY_NAME}}. Inclusion rationale: Log clearing is routinely observed before or after ransomware impact and is directly supported by Qilin. Threat-led context: Mandiant observed event-log clearing; Qilin supports it. Applicability=Windows; RansomwarePhase=Defense Impairment; Priority=High; Confidence=High. Scope boundary: TP-06 models the complete ransomware / disruptive extortion chain from perimeter or identity initial access through persistence, credential theft, privilege escalation, discovery, lateral movement, deployment, virtualization targeting, defense impairment, backup/recovery destruction, double-extortion collection/exfiltration, encryption/destruction and administrator lockout. It intentionally includes Windows, Linux, ESXi/virtualization and cloud-native ransomware paths because contemporary ransomware is no longer endpoint-only. Detailed identity-only compromise belongs to TP-01/TP-04, Partner Center/customer trusted access to TP-02/TP-03, software supply chain to TP-05, and data-theft-only/SaaS extortion is expanded in TP-09. This record is threat-profile intelligence and does not assert that the behavior occurred in a specific organisation.

data.Name: TP-06 | Disable or Modify System Firewall

data.Description: Disable or modify system firewall controls to permit RDP, SMB, SSH, tunneling or malware traffic. Why it matters for a system integrator/MSP: Mandiant observed attackers changing firewall rules to enable remote services and disabling ESXi firewalls before ransomware operations. Detection opportunities: Firewall disable/change; New RDP/SSH allow rule; Change by unusual admin. Defensive considerations: Protect management networks; Alert on firewall changes; Configuration enforcement.

data.Name: TP-06 | Safe Mode Boot
data.Source: X3M.AI Threat Profile - System Integrator - TP-06 Ransomware / Enterprise Disruption / Destructive Impact
data.Description: Force Windows into Safe Mode so third-party security tools may not start before ransomware execution. Why it matters for a system integrator/MSP: Safe Mode is a known ransomware defense-impairment technique and is currently represented as T1688 in ATT&CK v19. Applicability: Windows. Ransomware lifecycle phase: Pre-Impact Defense Impairment. Primary assets at risk: Windows endpoints, EDR. Detection opportunities: BCD Safe Mode changes; Unexpected Safe Mode reboot; Ransomware execution after reboot. Defensive considerations: Protect BCD changes; EDR tamper protection; Alert on safe mode configuration.
data.Notes: Threat Profile TP-06 | Generic System Integrator / MSP ransomware and destructive-impact profile | Organisation placeholder: {{COMPANY_NAME}}. Inclusion rationale: Safe Mode is a known ransomware defense-impairment technique and is currently represented as T1688 in ATT&CK v19. Threat-led context: Storm-0501-associated ransomware Embargo includes Safe Mode Boot. Applicability=Windows; RansomwarePhase=Pre-Impact Defense Impairment; Priority=Critical; Confidence=High. Scope boundary: TP-06 models the complete ransomware / disruptive extortion chain from perimeter or identity initial access through persistence, credential theft, privilege escalation, discovery, lateral movement, deployment, virtualization targeting, defense impairment, backup/recovery destruction, double-extortion collection/exfiltration, encryption/destruction and administrator lockout. It intentionally includes Windows, Linux, ESXi/virtualization and cloud-native ransomware paths because contemporary ransomware is no longer endpoint-only. Detailed identity-only compromise belongs to TP-01/TP-04, Partner Center/customer trusted access to TP-02/TP-03, software supply chain to TP-05, and data-theft-only/SaaS extortion is expanded in TP-09. This record is threat-profile intelligence and does not assert that the behavior occurred in a specific organisation.

data.Name: TP-06 | Modify Registry
data.Source: X3M.AI Threat Profile - System Integrator - TP-06 Ransomware / Enterprise Disruption / Destructive Impact
data.Description: Modify Windows Registry to disable Defender, enable credential caching, alter ransomware behavior or display ransom messages. Detection opportunities: Security-policy registry changes; Mass registry modification. Defensive considerations: Tamper protection; Registry monitoring; EDR.

data.Name: TP-06 | Inhibit System Recovery
data.Source: X3M.AI Threat Profile - System Integrator - TP-06 Ransomware / Enterprise Disruption / Destructive Impact
data.Description: Delete shadow copies, backups, snapshots, recovery catalogs or otherwise render recovery infrastructure unavailable. Why it matters for a system integrator/MSP: This is a defining ransomware technique. Recovery denial increases operational pressure and ransom leverage; backup infrastructure is deliberately targeted before encryption. Applicability: Core. Ransomware lifecycle phase: Anti-Recovery / Impact. Primary assets at risk: VSS, Backup repositories, Snapshots, Veeam, Commvault, Cohesity, vCenter backups. Detection opportunities: VSS deletion; Backup-volume deletion; Snapshot deletion; Backup service/console changes. Defensive considerations: Immutable/offline backups; Separate backup identity; MFA/PAM; Recovery tests; Network isolation.

data.Name: TP-06 | System Shutdown/Reboot
data.Source: X3M.AI Threat Profile - System Integrator - TP-06 Ransomware / Enterprise Disruption / Destructive Impact
data.Description: Shutdown or reboot systems to force encryption states, stop VMs, lock BitLocker-encrypted hosts or increase disruption. Why it matters for a system integrator/MSP: Mandiant observed automated VM shutdown and BitLocker deployments that scheduled reboot to force hosts into a locked state. Applicability: Core / Virtualization. Ransomware lifecycle phase: Pre-Impact / Impact. Primary assets at risk: Windows endpoints, Servers, Virtual machines, Hypervisors. Detection opportunities: Mass shutdown/reboot; Power-off via vCenter; Reboot shortly after BitLocker change. Defensive considerations: Alert on mass power actions; Separate virtualization admin; Change controls.
data.Notes: Threat Profile TP-06 | Generic System Integrator / MSP ransomware and destructive-impact profile | Organisation placeholder: {{COMPANY_NAME}}. Inclusion rationale: Mandiant observed automated VM shutdown and BitLocker deployments that scheduled reboot to force hosts into a locked state. Threat-led context: Mandiant observed VM shutdown and forced reboot; Qilin can shutdown/reboot systems. Applicability=Core / Virtualization; RansomwarePhase=Pre-Impact / Impact; Priority=Critical; Confidence=High. Scope boundary: TP-06 models the complete ransomware / disruptive extortion chain from perimeter or identity initial access through persistence, credential theft, privilege escalation, discovery, lateral movement, deployment, virtualization targeting, defense impairment, backup/recovery destruction, double-extortion collection/exfiltration, encryption/destruction and administrator lockout. It intentionally includes Windows, Linux, ESXi/virtualization and cloud-native ransomware paths because contemporary ransomware is no longer endpoint-only. Detailed identity-only compromise belongs to TP-01/TP-04, Partner Center/customer trusted access to TP-02/TP-03, software supply chain to TP-05, and data-theft-only/SaaS extortion is expanded in TP-09. This record is threat-profile intelligence and does not assert that the behavior occurred in a specific organisation.

data.Name: TP-06 | Data from Network Shared Drive
data.Source: X3M.AI Threat Profile - System Integrator - TP-06 Ransomware / Enterprise Disruption / Destructive Impact
data.Description: Collect files from network shares and NAS resources. Why it matters for a system integrator/MSP: File shares are high-value sources for both double extortion and ransomware encryption. Applicability: Core. Ransomware lifecycle phase: Collection. Primary assets at risk: File servers, NAS, Department shares, Project shares. Detection opportunities: Bulk share reads; Unusual recursive copy. Defensive considerations: Share least privilege; DLP; Monitor mass access.
data.Notes: Threat Profile TP-06 | Generic System Integrator / MSP ransomware and destructive-impact profile | Organisation placeholder: {{COMPANY_NAME}}. Inclusion rationale: File shares are high-value sources for both double extortion and ransomware encryption. Threat-led context: Technique included because it is structurally relevant to ransomware / enterprise disruption even where no specific current actor evidence is required. Applicability=Core; RansomwarePhase=Collection; Priority=Critical; Confidence=High. Scope boundary: TP-06 models the complete ransomware / disruptive extortion chain from perimeter or identity initial access through persistence, credential theft, privilege escalation, discovery, lateral movement, deployment, virtualization targeting, defense impairment, backup/recovery destruction, double-extortion collection/exfiltration, encryption/destruction and administrator lockout. It intentionally includes Windows, Linux, ESXi/virtualization and cloud-native ransomware paths because contemporary ransomware is no longer endpoint-only. Detailed identity-only compromise belongs to TP-01/TP-04, Partner Center/customer trusted access to TP-02/TP-03, software supply chain to TP-05, and data-theft-only/SaaS extortion is expanded in TP-09. This record is threat-profile intelligence and does not assert that the behavior occurred in a specific organisation.

data.Name: TP-06 | Data from Information Repositories: Databases
data.Source: X3M.AI Threat Profile - System Integrator - TP-06 Ransomware / Enterprise Disruption / Destructive Impact
data.Description: Collect or export database content for extortion or business disruption. Why it matters for a system integrator/MSP: Database exports can contain highly concentrated personal, financial and customer data. Applicability: Database. Ransomware lifecycle phase: Collection. Primary assets at risk: SQL databases, Application databases, ERP data. Detection opportunities: Large export; Import/Export Wizard usage; Unusual bulk SELECT. Defensive considerations: Database auditing; PAM; DLP.
data.Notes: Threat Profile TP-06 | Generic System Integrator / MSP ransomware and destructive-impact profile | Organisation placeholder: {{COMPANY_NAME}}. Inclusion rationale: Database exports can contain highly concentrated personal, financial and customer data. Threat-led context: Mandiant observed SQL Server Import and Export Wizard used to export a database. Applicability=Database; RansomwarePhase=Collection; Priority=High; Confidence=High. Scope boundary: TP-06 models the complete ransomware / disruptive extortion chain from perimeter or identity initial access through persistence, credential theft, privilege escalation, discovery, lateral movement, deployment, virtualization targeting, defense impairment, backup/recovery destruction, double-extortion collection/exfiltration, encryption/destruction and administrator lockout. It intentionally includes Windows, Linux, ESXi/virtualization and cloud-native ransomware paths because contemporary ransomware is no longer endpoint-only. Detailed identity-only compromise belongs to TP-01/TP-04, Partner Center/customer trusted access to TP-02/TP-03, software supply chain to TP-05, and data-theft-only/SaaS extortion is expanded in TP-09. This record is threat-profile intelligence and does not assert that the behavior occurred in a specific organisation.

data.Description: Retrieve files and objects from Azure Storage, OneDrive or other cloud stores before destruction/encryption. data.Name: TP-06 | Archive Collected Data: Archive via Utility
data.Source: X3M.AI Threat Profile - System Integrator - TP-06 Ransomware / Enterprise Disruption / Destructive Impact
data.Description: Use WinRAR, 7-Zip or other utilities to compress data before exfiltration. Why it matters for a system integrator/MSP: WinRAR use increased materially in 2025 ransomware incidents and is a common pre-exfiltration behavior. Applicability: Core. Ransomware lifecycle phase: Collection / Staging. Primary assets at risk: Sensitive data, Archives, Staging host. Detection opportunities: Large archive creation; Portable WinRAR/7z from admin path. Defensive considerations: DLP; EDR; Monitor archive utilities.
data.Notes: Threat Profile TP-06 | Generic System Integrator / MSP ransomware and destructive-impact profile | Organisation placeholder: {{COMPANY_NAME}}. data.Description: Automatically transfer selected file types or staged archives to attacker infrastructure. Why it matters for a system integrator/MSP: Automation shortens dwell time and enables large-scale double-extortion theft before encryption. Applicability: Core. Ransomware lifecycle phase: Exfiltration. Primary assets at risk: Sensitive documents, Archives. Detection opportunities: Scripted recurring transfer; File-extension-filtered exfiltration. Defensive considerations: DLP; Network egress control.
data.Notes: Threat Profile TP-06 | Generic System Integrator / MSP ransomware and destructive-impact profile | Organisation placeholder: {{COMPANY_NAME}}. Inclusion rationale: Automation shortens dwell time and enables large-scale double-extortion theft before encryption. Threat-led context: Mandiant observed scripted Rclone transfers selecting common file extensions. Applicability=Core; RansomwarePhase=Exfiltration; Priority=High; Confidence=High. Scope boundary: TP-06 models the complete ransomware / disruptive extortion chain from perimeter or identity initial access through persistence, credential theft, privilege escalation, discovery, lateral movement, deployment, virtualization targeting, defense impairment, backup/recovery destruction, double-extortion collection/exfiltration, encryption/destruction and administrator lockout. It intentionally includes Windows, Linux, ESXi/virtualization and cloud-native ransomware paths because contemporary ransomware is no longer endpoint-only. Detailed identity-only compromise belongs to TP-01/TP-04, Partner Center/customer trusted access to TP-02/TP-03, software supply chain to TP-05, and data-theft-only/SaaS extortion is expanded in TP-09. This record is threat-profile intelligence and does not assert that the behavior occurred in a specific organisation.

data.Name: TP-06 | Modify Cloud Compute Infrastructure: Delete Cloud Instance
data.Source: X3M.AI Threat Profile - System Integrator - TP-06 Ransomware / Enterprise Disruption / Destructive Impact
data.Description: Delete cloud VMs or instances after malicious activity or as part of destructive impact. Why it matters for a system integrator/MSP: Cloud administrative access can convert ransomware/extortion into direct infrastructure destruction and loss of forensic evidence. Applicability: Cloud. Ransomware lifecycle phase: Cloud Destruction. Primary assets at risk: Cloud VMs, Compute instances. Detection opportunities: Bulk instance deletion; Delete operations by unusual admin. Defensive considerations: Resource locks; PIM; Protected recovery; Alert on delete.

data.Name: TP-06 | Modify Cloud Compute Infrastructure: Modify Cloud Compute Configurations
data.Source: X3M.AI Threat Profile - System Integrator - TP-06 Ransomware / Enterprise Disruption / Destructive Impact
data.Description: Modify compute settings, policies or configurations to weaken protections or facilitate destructive operations. Why it matters for a system integrator/MSP: Cloud ransomware actors can use legitimate management APIs to change workload configuration before deletion or encryption. Applicability: Cloud. Ransomware lifecycle phase: Cloud Defense Impairment. Primary assets at risk: VM configuration, Cloud policy, Compute controls. Detection opportunities: Unusual compute configuration changes; Security settings modified before impact. Defensive considerations: PIM; Resource policy; Alert on critical config changes.

data.Name: TP-06 | Data Encrypted for Impact
data.Source: X3M.AI Threat Profile - System Integrator - TP-06 Ransomware / Enterprise Disruption / Destructive Impact
data.Description: Encrypt files, virtual disks, cloud storage objects or entire systems to deny availability and extort payment. Why it matters for a system integrator/MSP: This is the defining ransomware impact technique. Current ATT&CK includes traditional hosts, ESXi VMFS datastores and cloud-storage object encryption. Qilin supports Windows, Linux and ESXi. Applicability: Core. Ransomware lifecycle phase: Impact. Primary assets at risk: Endpoints, Servers, File shares, ESXi datastores, Cloud storage, Databases. Detection opportunities: High-rate file rewrites/renames; VM disk encryption; Cloud object rewrite/encryption; BitLocker mass enablement. Defensive considerations: Ransomware protection; Immutable backups; Segmentation; EDR; Storage versioning.

data.Name: TP-06 | Data Destruction
data.Source: X3M.AI Threat Profile - System Integrator - TP-06 Ransomware / Enterprise Disruption / Destructive Impact
data.Description: Delete or irreversibly destroy data and systems rather than or in addition to encrypting them. Why it matters for a system integrator/MSP: Ransomware/extortion operations increasingly combine encryption with destructive actions against backups, identity and infrastructure to increase pressure. Applicability: Core / Destructive. Ransomware lifecycle phase: Impact. Primary assets at risk: Business data, Cloud resources, Backups, Servers. Detection opportunities: Mass deletion; Destructive commands; Wiper-like activity. Defensive considerations: Immutable backups; Protected recovery identities; Deletion protection.
data.Notes: Threat Profile TP-06 | Generic System Integrator / MSP ransomware and destructive-impact profile | Organisation placeholder: {{COMPANY_NAME}}. Inclusion rationale: Ransomware/extortion operations increasingly combine encryption with destructive actions against backups, identity and infrastructure to increase pressure. Threat-led context: Technique included because it is structurally relevant to ransomware / enterprise disruption even where no specific current actor evidence is required. Applicability=Core / Destructive; RansomwarePhase=Impact; Priority=Critical; Confidence=High. Scope boundary: TP-06 models the complete ransomware / disruptive extortion chain from perimeter or identity initial access through persistence, credential theft, privilege escalation, discovery, lateral movement, deployment, virtualization targeting, defense impairment, backup/recovery destruction, double-extortion collection/exfiltration, encryption/destruction and administrator lockout. It intentionally includes Windows, Linux, ESXi/virtualization and cloud-native ransomware paths because contemporary ransomware is no longer endpoint-only. Detailed identity-only compromise belongs to TP-01/TP-04, Partner Center/customer trusted access to TP-02/TP-03, software supply chain to TP-05, and data-theft-only/SaaS extortion is expanded in TP-09. This record is threat-profile intelligence and does not assert that the behavior occurred in a specific organisation.

data.Name: TP-06 | Defacement: Internal Defacement
data.Source: X3M.AI Threat Profile - System Integrator - TP-06 Ransomware / Enterprise Disruption / Destructive Impact
data.Description: Modify desktop wallpaper, logon banners or other internal content to display ransom instructions. Why it matters for a system integrator/MSP: Internal defacement communicates impact to users and can accompany or follow encryption. Applicability: Core. Ransomware lifecycle phase: Impact. Primary assets at risk: Desktop wallpaper, Login banners, Internal systems. Detection opportunities: Mass wallpaper/banner changes; Registry LegalNotice modifications. Defensive considerations: Configuration monitoring.

data.Name: TP-06 | Account Access Removal
data.Source: X3M.AI Threat Profile - System Integrator - TP-06 Ransomware / Enterprise Disruption / Destructive Impact
data.Description: Disable, delete or reset legitimate administrator accounts to delay containment and recovery. Why it matters for a system integrator/MSP: Identity lockout can protect attacker persistence, block responders and amplify business outage during ransomware or cloud extortion. Applicability: Cloud / Identity / AD. Ransomware lifecycle phase: Impact / Response Inhibition. Primary assets at risk: Global admins, Domain admins, Security responders, Backup administrators. Detection opportunities: Privileged account disable/delete; Bulk password reset; Role removal. Defensive considerations: Emergency-access accounts; Out-of-band recovery; Alert on admin removal.

data.Name: TP-06 | Financial Theft
data.Source: X3M.AI Threat Profile - System Integrator - TP-06 Ransomware / Enterprise Disruption / Destructive Impact
data.Description: Demand payment for decryption, restoration or to prevent publication of stolen data. Why it matters for a system integrator/MSP: Financial extortion is the business objective of ransomware-as-a-service operations and directly converts technical disruption and stolen data into monetary pressure. Applicability: Core. Ransomware lifecycle phase: Extortion / Impact. Primary assets at risk: Organisation finances, Reputation, Stolen data, Operational continuity. Detection opportunities: Ransom note; Negotiation communication; Leak-site publication. Defensive considerations: Incident response plan; Legal/law enforcement engagement; Recovery capability; Data-loss controls.
data.Notes: Threat Profile TP-06 | Generic System Integrator / MSP ransomware and destructive-impact profile | Organisation placeholder: {{COMPANY_NAME}}. Inclusion rationale: Financial extortion is the business objective of ransomware-as-a-service operations and directly converts technical disruption and stolen data into monetary pressure. Threat-led context: Water Galura/Qilin uses double extortion: payment for decryption and non-publication of stolen data. Applicability=Core; RansomwarePhase=Extortion / Impact; Priority=Critical; Confidence=High. Scope boundary: TP-06 models the complete ransomware / disruptive extortion chain from perimeter or identity initial access through persistence, credential theft, privilege escalation, discovery, lateral movement, deployment, virtualization targeting, defense impairment, backup/recovery destruction, double-extortion collection/exfiltration, encryption/destruction and administrator lockout. It intentionally includes Windows, Linux, ESXi/virtualization and cloud-native ransomware paths because contemporary ransomware is no longer endpoint-only. Detailed identity-only compromise belongs to TP-01/TP-04, Partner Center/customer trusted access to TP-02/TP-03, software supply chain to TP-05, and data-theft-only/SaaS extortion is expanded in TP-09. This record is threat-profile intelligence and does not assert that the behavior occurred in a specific organisation.
